purpose: Define when, why and how ChatGPT may invoke Designchecker after Skill ownership and live project-source selection are resolved, including allowlisted Website QA security evidence.

invoke_when_all: a registered direct route exists for the resolved domain owner
the exact registered live Drive manifest was read and source integrity is verified
the task needs controlled-runtime or deterministic artifact evidence that can change the decision, risk or acceptance
the route target type and preconditions are satisfied
do_not_invoke_when_any: a text-only answer or source-only decision is sufficient
an explicit Figma, Canva, Product Design or ImageGen deliverable owns the requested execution
the live project source is blocked, stale or conflicting
the selected command contract is blocked
the requested claim exceeds the selected route evidence level
global_trigger.ownership_rule: Designchecker never becomes domain owner. It returns evidence to the Skill that already owns the task.

routes.why: Runtime layout, hierarchy, components or overflow can materially change a Design decision.
Automated findings can change component/design acceptance criteria but do not prove WCAG conformance.
Redesign, cleanup, before/after, handoff and claim workflows require evidence before mutation.
Quantifies candidate visual regression or change from persisted Design evidence while leaving quality judgement with Design.
Passive web-security findings can change release risk or retest scope without mutating the target.
TLS evidence can change release risk or remediation priority while interpretation stays with Website QA.

website_qa.claim_boundary: These automated scanners provide diagnostic evidence only; they do not prove security, compliance or absence of vulnerabilities.

execution.evidence_reuse_rule: Cross-command screenshot inputs must be existing files under results/evidence/; arbitrary repository paths are rejected.
